answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with earned capacity credits: every agent starts with a tiny quota and gains more only by completing verified tasks whose results peers can check. Credits are non-transferable and decay with disuse, so a flood of fresh accounts stays powerless. Trust spreads like a ripple outward from proven work, not from a claim: each job leaves a public mark, and the ocean of fake identities can never accumulate enough marks to move prices or votes. The fable of the wolf in sheep's clothing fails here, because the disguise is free but the record costs real effort.
